subsystems.name: Code definition
subsystems.role: specifies the sparse parity-check matrices that define which qubit errors are detected.

subsystems.name: Qubit mapping and connectivity
subsystems.role: places code qubits on physical qubits so the required stabilizer measurements can be performed.

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction
subsystems.role: measures stabilizers repeatedly to detect errors without collapsing the encoded information.

subsystems.name: Classical decoder
subsystems.role: turns syndrome history into a predicted error correction.

subsystems.name: Logical operations
subsystems.role: performs gates on the encoded logical qubits while keeping them protected.

subsystems.name: Hardware platform
subsystems.role: provides the physical qubits and control needed to run the code.

buildSteps.title: Select code parameters
buildSteps.detail: Choose a qLDPC family, such as hypergraph product or lifted product codes, and tune n, k and d for a target physical error rate.

buildSteps.title: Map to hardware
buildSteps.detail: Assign code qubits to physical qubits, inserting SWAPs or using shuttling to realise the sparse but non-local stabilizer measurements.

buildSteps.title: Compile syndrome extraction
buildSteps.detail: Schedule ancilla qubits and two-qubit gates into a fault-tolerant circuit, verifying that a single fault cannot spread into an uncorrectable error.

buildSteps.title: Implement the decoder
buildSteps.detail: Build a classical decoder, for example belief propagation with ordered-statistics post-processing, and optimise it to process syndromes in real time.

buildSteps.title: Validate on small codes
buildSteps.detail: Run the smallest instances on a handful of physical qubits to confirm that logical error rate falls as code distance grows.

buildSteps.title: Scale up distance
buildSteps.detail: Increase code size and distance while improving gate fidelities and connectivity, aiming to operate below the code threshold.

buildSteps.title: Add logical gates
buildSteps.detail: Demonstrate logical operations and error correction together, showing that encoded information outlives the physical qubits used to store it.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate overhead advantage
buildSteps.detail: Compare physical qubit counts per logical qubit against the surface code for the same logical error rate.

prerequisites.why: qLDPC codes need error rates well below 0.1% to beat the surface code, and current hardware is still improving.

prerequisites.tech: Qubit connectivity for sparse long-range interactions
prerequisites.why: trapped ions can shuttle and superconducting circuits have limited coupling; qLDPC codes require a specific interaction graph.
belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding is known, but must run fast enough for large codes.
circuits have been designed and tested on small codes, but not at the scale needed for a logical qubit.

prerequisites.tech: Sufficient physical qubit count and control
prerequisites.why: current devices have tens to hundreds of qubits; useful qLDPC codes may need thousands.

prerequisites.tech: Error rates below the code threshold
prerequisites.why: no experiment has yet shown a qLDPC code operating below threshold with increasing distance.

pathway.milestone: small-scale syndrome extraction and decoding on trapped-ion hardware
pathway.unlocks: proof that qLDPC codes work on real devices.

pathway.milestone: a single logical qubit with lower error rate than its best physical qubit using a qLDPC code
pathway.unlocks: evidence of an overhead advantage over the surface code.

pathway.milestone: multiple logical qubits with logical gates and real-time decoding
pathway.unlocks: building blocks for a fault-tolerant processor.

pathway.milestone: fault-tolerant quantum computers using qLDPC codes with roughly tenfold fewer physical qubits
pathway.unlocks: practical quantum algorithms for chemistry, materials and cryptography.
